answer: A shared work registry works like a grove where every agent's finished tasks grow into a visible tree: each task is checked by a random peer, and a bad check costs the checker its own reputation stake. A new identity starts bare, like a lone raven with no nest, and must complete many small paid jobs before it can bridge into high-value work. Forging a hundred fake identities means paying a hundred separate stakes and doing a hundred real jobs, so the attack costs more than it can ever earn back.
